coverage.r1: Diarization is badly fragmented: many one-word turns, '?' labels, and Medi/Amal labels swapped inside the verb drill (e.g. [01:52]-[01:55] '?' lines are Medi's sentence; [02:16] 'Medi: طريقة؟' is Amal's recast being echoed). Long English-only stretches: 11:02-20:30 (AI/method talk), 23:00-25:00 (beekeeper at the door, English), 36:44-40:55 and 44:55-50:30 (meta talk about the verb). Latin-transliterated Arabic from 12:27 to 29:30 and 36:37 to 1:00:40 (very low quality: 'babysit'=ببسط, 'biscuit'=بنبسط, 'button visit'=بتنبسط, 'Investii'=انبسطي); 25:05-25:38 is garbled beyond safe reading ('ana bihna binkhales al-asal', 'shay na'na' ma asal mufrad') and is not scored. No CHAT lines in this transcript. Pronunciation-only fixes left out as S4: 'luka' for لغة [00:57-00:59], بسّتني for بسطني [30:35-30:37], بيسبت/بنسبت/'ban sebet' letter-order swaps for بيبسط/بنبسط [32:30, 34:21, 56:04-56:13, 1:01:44], stress on the T in 'in basatu' [55:25]. 30:00-53:00 is a conjugation drill of بسط/انبسط; drill rows are written only where she recast a form. His own self-fixes (إسباني 04:47, بيسبت 32:30, basatini 41:09, mabsut 27:54) are not written.
coverage.r2: Diarization very fragmented; many Medi fragments carry the ? label (e.g. 01:52 'أنا لقيت الطريق', 35:58-36:05 بسات/بَسْتَكْ, 58:11 betenbesti) - judged from content. 11:16-20:30 is English-only planning talk; 22:49-24:55 is a honey-seller interruption in English. 12:27-13:16, 20:31-30:25, 36:23-42:50 and 45:12-59:56 are Latin-transliterated by the engine, so ط/ت and vowel differences (basat/beset, F2/F3) are unreadable there; I skipped those as pronunciation. Root-letter slips (34:21 بنسبت, 56:04 ban sebet, 1:01:34 بيسبط) treated as S4 per brief, not rows. 13:16 'sehel ktir' -> her 'Ktir sehel?' left out (both orders acceptable). 44:44 ابستههم -> her أبستيهم 'Good' left out (unclear whether a fix or a feminine variant). 00:39 'software لقة' too garbled to file beyond the لغة didn't-know.

r3_note: Diarization is badly fragmented (many '?:' lines) and 20:30-59:30 is Latin-transliterated, so several Latin forms cannot be told apart (e.g. 'Bihteb' is used for Amal's own bit7eb at 25:11). Merger notes: (1) D10 and D24 were mis-paired - r1's D10 half (akun -> 3am baseer, B14) is the SAME row as r2's D24; I kept D10 as r2's aswad->sayyi2 vocab row and D24 as the B14 row, so nothing is doubled. (2) D12/D13: r1 split the 53:36 line into two pieces (ending -ti, preposition bi/fi) and r2 wrote one row covering the preposition; I kept D12 = ending piece (B5) and D13 = preposition piece (D2); r2's D12 half is folded into D13. (3) D17/D32: r1's D17 row is really the laiti piece (= D32); I kept D17 as the haketili piece (r2) and D32 as laiti. (4) D28 (32:30 بيسبت -> بيبسط) and the letter-order part of D15 are the ب/س root-letter swap that READER-BRIEF names as S4 (بنسبت for بنبسط); same slip recurs at 34:21 and 1:01:34. (5) Candidates I did NOT add because they are probably already in the agreed list - please check: 08:36 'بعيد الـ نفس مش الـ' -> 'نفس المشكلة' (A2), 12:54 'el ghayr tariqa' -> 'Not el, just ghayr' (A2), 55:52 'Bi safar hom' -> 'Safartom' (A3), 59:45 'Investii yomek' -> 'Bee Yomeek' (D2), 1:01:23 'الأكتر إشي' -> 'No أل just أكتر إشي' (C3), 1:02:23 'بيسبط' -> 'ببسّط' (B18). Also 04:19-04:26 بهمس/بتحمس -> متحمس (B15) is a separate fix from D19.

rows.medi_said: الأحسن

rows.medi_said: To learn would be أتأل-- or يتعلّم
rows.why: In 'شو أحسن طريقة ... to learn' he offered the he-form يتعلّم; she said لا, أتعلم (I-form); he then asked 'is that for me or just to learn?' and she said Both - the fix is the person prefix, a bucket rule, so grammar not a didn't-know (he knows the verb: sheet 'i learn | Ana bat3allam').

rows.medi_said: Okay. أتعلم لغة جديد

rows.medi_said: مع عربي فلسطيني. آم

rows.medi_said: بس إذا إذا بقدر آم أصلح

rows.medi_said: بقدر آم أصلح، أصلحه آم…

rows.medi_said: I excited؟ أنا بهمس.

rows.medi_said: embasana.

rows.medi_said: Embassatet il hafla.

rows.medi_said: al. Bi safar hom

rows.medi_said: Inti beten bestiti

rows.medi_said: More, more happy? ... Oh, the most happy. Did you say أحسن or أكثر؟ أحسن right?
rows.amal_said: The most. The most. ... شو أكتر إشي. ... No. The best thing is أحسن إشي.
rows.why: Her question 'shoo aktar ishi biebsitak' (1:00:46): he read aktar ishi as 'more' (1:01:02), she said 'The most'; he then guessed she had said أحسن (1:01:07) and she said No, شو أكتر إشي, the best thing is أحسن إشي (1:01:15); one listening miss of the sheet item 'the most | Aktar shee | أكتر شيء'.
rows.english: what is the thing that makes you happiest?
rows.r3_why: Both readers describe the same listening miss from different lines; merged into one row anchored at the first wrong reading (1:01:02) with the أحسن follow-up in the quote.

rows.medi_said: So الأكتر إشي-
rows.why: el- never goes in front of the comparative aktar; she said 'No أل just أكتر إشي'.

rows.medi_said: إلي right؟
rows.why: He wanted to insert illi after aktar ishi before the verb; she said there is no illi here.
rows.english: the thing that makes me happiest

rows.medi_said: أكتر إشي بيس– بيسبط–
rows.amal_said: بيسبتني- بيب... بي and then س
rows.why: 'the thing that makes ME happy' needs the object -ni; her first move was to add it to his word (بيسبتني) before walking him through the letter order; he reached بيبسطني at 1:01:50 (ممتاز); low because his line is cut off (بيسبط–) so he may have been about to add -ni, and the ب/س order part is S4 (brief: بنسبت for بنبسط).
rows.english: the thing that makes me happy the most
rows.r3_why: Only r1 wrote it; she did supply the -ni, but his line is cut mid-word, so real-but-unprovable, kept at low.

rows.medi_said: بيبسطني لماaa would this be conditional؟ لما بكون في الطبيعة؟
rows.why: No b- after lamma: akoon not bakoon; she recast and he repeated 'لما اكون' at 1:02:13 ('I knew it was conditional but I got past it').

rows.medi_said: to make someone happy is آآá بيسبط.
rows.amal_said: ببسّط. ... No و and الب goes-- I should make you record just ببسط، ببسط
rows.why: She wanted the I-form ببسّط (I make happy) and he gave the he-prefix بيـ; the س/ب order is S4 and she also drilled the sound, so the person error is the only gradable part.

rows.medi_said: عافيا فيكي. شكرًا.
rows.why: Reply to her يعطيك العافية (1:03:03) is the set phrase الله يعافيكي; he produced a made-up shape of the same word (عافية/يعافي), so a wrong form of a word he knows (tier 2) rather than a different word; she let it pass; the reply is not on her sheet (only 'ya'tiki al'afyah | يعطيكي العافية').
rows.r3_why: Both readers agree it is vocab-B and low; the transcript shows a mangled form of the right word, which the brief files as tier 2.
